Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Greenbridge is moving quickly through procurement and the security/compliance team asked for details on how Redwood measures uptime and latency (SLOs), how those are instrumented, and what customer-facing access we get to telemetry.

Specifically they asked for:
- A one-page matrix listing SLO definitions (availability, p99/p95 latency), measurement windows, and the source of truth for the metric.
- Where the alerts originate and how we (customer) receive incident notifications.
- Whether customers can view the live dashboards or receive historical exports (90/365 day retention).

Could you send a short matrix and a screenshot of the dashboard we can share with compliance? Also cc'ing our SRE, Tom, for any follow-ups.

Appreciate it — Meera

Hi Meera — thanks, happy to provide. I'm attaching a concise SLO measurement matrix and a Grafana screenshot that mirrors the customer portal view. High level:

- Availability SLO: monthly rolling window, measured by internal request success rate (5xx and critical error filters). Source of truth: system-level aggregator (Prometheus -> long-term store).
- Latency SLOs: p95/p99 measured at the API gateway after routing and client-side retry normalization. Window: 7-day and 30-day baselines for alerts, 30/90-day for reporting.
- Alerts: primary alerts are emitted from our alerting rules in Prometheus/Alertmanager and routed to PagerDuty; customers can subscribe to a webhooks feed or SAML-backed webhook for incident updates.

I've attached the matrix (slo-measurement-matrix.xlsx) and a dashboard screenshot. Rishi can add the instrumentation caveats and the exception path for unusual retention or custom thresholds.

Next steps: if Greenbridge needs a temporary exception to our standard retention or wants a read-only Grafana invite tied to an SSO assertion, we'll take it through our procurement/security exception form (attached) and a brief security review.

Thanks — Stephanie

Hi Meera + team — quick technical follow-up from our side. A few clarifications to help your security team evaluate:

1) Measurement methodology
- Availability: we count successful token-authenticated requests to the inference API. Excluded are scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified) and known downstream outages that we detect via dependency health checks.
- Latency: we compute e2e server-side latency using gateway ingress -> response send timestamps. Retries are collapsed (we normalize to the original client request to avoid inflation).

2) Instrumentation and retention
- Primary metrics are stored in Prometheus (90 days) and materialized to a long-term store (Parquet on S3) for 365-day retention for enterprise contracts.
- If Greenbridge requires longer retention or different aggregation buckets, that is handled as an amendment to the contract and goes through our exception review.

3) Customer access
- Out of the box: read-only Grafana view of your tenant-scoped dashboards (SSO + role-based access).
- Exports: CSV/PARQUET exports available on request via support ticket (we can automate periodic exports).

4) Alerts and notification patterns
- We emit platform alerts (availability degradation, p99 latency breach, error-rate spikes). Customers can request to subscribe via:
  a) PagerDuty integration (we add the service under your PD account), or
  b) Webhook delivery (signed payloads), or
  c) Email + aggregated postmortem to the security contact list.

If you want, I can attach the raw alert rules or a sanitized playbook.

— Rishi

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our SRE side:

- For the availability SLO, can you confirm whether internal retries (within Redwood) are visible or collapsed in the dashboard we would be given? We need to be able to attribute retries during transient infra blips.
- For alerting, can we get an SLA on alert delivery (e.g., webhook delivery retries / expected window to receive an alert)? Our SOC wants to know about delivery guarantees.

Also, on exports: would the CSV export include raw request-level histograms (for us to compute our own percentiles), or is it aggregated only?

If it helps, I can schedule a short call with our security folks — want to loop in Laura from Redwood who owns the procurement checklist.

Hi Tom / Meera — looping in the procurement track items so we don't block your review. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Retries: the tenant-scoped dashboard will show both raw and normalized metrics. By default the customer view shows normalized latency (retries collapsed) but we can expose a raw trace histogram on request for your exported reports. That option is part of the GBH enterprise package and would be called out in the order form.
- Alert delivery SLA: webhook retries are attempted for 24 hours with exponential backoff; we surface delivery status in the tenant audit log and will provide a signed delivery report on request for procurement. For PagerDuty the integration follows PD best practices; we guarantee notification handoff to PD within 60s when the alert rule fires (subject to network conditions).
- Exports: we can provide request-level histograms for a rolling 90-day window in Parquet format; full 365-day raw exports require an addendum.

Action items:
1) Stephanie: share the completed exception form if Greenbridge wants a read-only Grafana invite before contract signature.
2) Meera/Tom: confirm whether you want raw histograms in the initial 90-day export.
3) I'll prepare a short procurement appendix that lists the exact wording for retention/alert SLAs to include in the order form.

Laura Bennett
